get.description: Retrieves the names of all projects that exist in your AWR account.

post.description: This operation creates a new project in your AWR account. You can specify the project details such as country, search depth and update frequency. You must add at least one website, one keyword and one search engine.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The name your project will have in your account. Use URL encoding if you want to add spaces in the name.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Used for formatting numbers and gathering AdWords country-specific data. Use Alpha-2 codes from: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2#Officially_assigned_code_elements.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: The number of pages to be retrieved from search engines. You can specify a number from 1 to 10 (pages).  Leave this field blank to use the default (2 pages).

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Your project's update frequency.

aliases.description: Comma separated list of values, eg: *.yahoo.com,yahoo.com,subdomain.yahoo.com,yahoo.com/URL*,yahoo.com/URL,https://www.youtube.com/c/YahooChannel

google.description: Use this object to add a Google search engine.

name.description: This field allows you to add a Google search engine with or without location. If you don't add a location or language, the default is google.com United States in english.

country.description:
You can find a list of all countries here: https://www.advancedwebranking.com/cloud/api/countries.csv
Use the short form with two letters. Example: DE (for Germany).

se_type.description: This is the search engine vertical.

language.description:
You can find a list of all languages here: https://www.advancedwebranking.com/cloud/api/languages.csv
Use the short form with two letters. Example: de (for German).

location.description:
You can find a list of all locations here: https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/data/geotargets.
Example: San Francisco, CA.

other.description: Use this object to add any other predefined search engines.

awr_id.description:
Here you can add any other predefined search engine. The full list of search engines that AWR supports is here: https://app.advancedwebranking.com/searchengines
Add only the search engine ID from the third column in the list. Example: 1287784873 (for Google Play).

get.description: Schedules a top sites export for a single project.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The name of the project in your account.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: The oldest date, yyyy-mm-dd format.

parameters.name: stopDate
parameters.description: The most recent date, yyyy-mm-dd format.

parameters.name: encodeurl
parameters.description: Whether to encode URLs.

parameters.name: topUrls
parameters.description: How many URLs to export for each page.

parameters.name: searchEngine
parameters.description: JSON array with one or multiple search Engine IDs: [1, 2, 3]. Leave it out to get data for all search engines.

parameters.name: keywordGroupId
parameters.description: Alternative to keywordGroupName. JSON array with one or multiple keyword group IDs: [1, 2, 3]. Leave it out to get data for All Keywords.

parameters.name: keywordGroupName
parameters.description: Alternative to keywordGroupId. JSON array with one or multiple keyword group names: ["keyword group 1", "keyword group 2", "keyword group 3"]. Leave it out to get data for All Search Engines.

parameters.name: sponsored
parameters.description: Whether to include sponsored results in your export.

parameters.name: resultType
parameters.description: JSON array with one or more result types to include. If set, your export will only include these types. Possible values: ads bottom, ads shop, ads top, aggregator units, ai overviews, app, buying guides, carousel, deals, direct answer, discussions & forums, events, explore brands, faq, featured snippets (includes all subtypes: paragraph, list, table, video), featured snippets list, featured snippets paragraph, featured snippets table, featured snippets video, filter by sidebar, flights, how-to, images, interesting finds, jobs, knowledge panel, local pack, multi image thumbnails, organic, people also ask, product knowledge panel, products, q&a, recipes, related products, reviews, single image thumbnails, sitelinks, sponsored (can only be added if the sponsored parameter is not set to false), top stories, tweets, videos, visual stories. Example: ["featured snippets paragraph", "featured snippets list"].

parameters.name: pixelPosition
parameters.description: Whether to include the Pixel Position column in your export.

parameters.name: xlsx
parameters.description: Whether to export an XLSX instead of a CSV.

parameters.name: addPixelHeight
parameters.description: Whether to add the Pixel Height column.

parameters.name: addClickShare
parameters.description: Whether to add the Click Share column.

post.description: This operation adds or removes websites, keywords, competitors or search engines in a project. It can also change the search depth or the update frequency.

project.description:
Your project's name as shown in your AWR account.
Use URL encoding, for example: "My Project/DE" => "My Project%2FDE".

aliases.description: Comma separated list of values, example: .yahoo.com,yahoo.com,subdomain.yahoo.com,yahoo.com/URL,yahoo.com/URL,https://www.youtube.com/c/YahooChannel

addSearchengines.description: This allows you to add search engines to your project.

google.description: Use this object to add a Google search engine.

name.description: This field allows you to add a Google search engine with or without location. If you don't add a location or language, the default is google.com United States in english.

country.description:
You can find a list of all countries here: https://www.advancedwebranking.com/cloud/api/countries.csv
Use the short form with two letters. Example: DE (for Germany).

se_type.description: This is the search engine vertical.

language.description:
You can find a list of all languages here: https://www.advancedwebranking.com/cloud/api/languages.csv
Use the short form with two letters. Example: de (for German).

location.description:
You can find a list of all locations here: https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/data/geotargets.
Example: San Francisco, CA.

other.description: Use this object to add any other predefined search engines.

awr_id.description:
Here you can add any other predefined search engine. The full list of search engines that AWR supports is here: https://app.advancedwebranking.com/searchengines
Add only the search engine ID from the third column in the list. Example: 1287784873 (for Google Play).

removeSearchengines.description: This allows you to remove search engines from your project.

awr_id.description: Enter the id of the search engine you want to delete. You can find all search engines ids from your project from this API: https://awr.readme.io/reference/get-project-details
